question: A 60-W lightbulb operates on a 120-V source. What is the current flowing through the bulb?
solution:
The correct answer is __0.5 A**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Power formula:__ Power (P) = Voltage (V) × Current (I).
 
• Given power is 60 W and voltage is 120 V.
 
• Using the formula, Current (I) = Power (P) / Voltage (V).
 
• Current (I) = 60 / 120 = 0.5 A.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is 0.5 A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that Voltage (V) = Current (I) × Resistance (R).
 
• It provides a relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in an electrical circuit.
 
 
 
• **Power in Electrical Circuits:**
 
 
• Electrical power is measured in watts (W).
 
• It represents the rate at which electrical energy is converted into another form of energy.
